# Plan: three width tiers for the page shell and screen 24 (09/10/2026)

This plan builds the part of spec section 4.4 that plan B cut (ruling R-B1): widths from 768 to 1279
(tablet) and below 768 (phone). Reason: the product owner opened screen 24 on a phone in Chrome and
the whole page broke (FE-23 in `spec/frontend-brainstorm-log.md`). Run under FE-21: the controller decides on its own,
following the recommendations, records the decisions here, does not stop to ask for approval; no commit (the product owner commits).

## Defects measured before the fix (09/10/2026, the `dist-e2e` build rebuilt the same day)

Measuring script: captures and measures Meridian's screen 24 with Playwright (Chromium emulating Pixel 7 and WebKit emulating
iPhone 15, plus the widths 360, 768, 1024, 1280), in both languages.

| Width | Measurement |
|---|---|
| 412 (Pixel 7) | Chrome shrinks the page by itself: the window becomes 948 px (English), 962 px (Vietnamese), the text is left at about 43% of its real size |
| 393 (iPhone 15) | The document is 946 px wide, 21 elements lie beyond the right edge (search box, New, Help, bell, language selector, Change request button, five tabs, screen title) |
| 360 | Same as Pixel 7: the window becomes 949 px |
| 768 | The document is 948 px wide; the bell, language selector and screen title lie beyond the right edge |
| 1024 and 1280 | No overflow |

Screenshots: the project name is broken one letter per line because the page column is left with only 180 px (412 minus the sidebar 232); the buttons of the
header overlap the title. 54 controls are smaller than 44 x 44 at phone width.

Root cause: no component reads the screen width. The sidebar is always `sidebarW` 232 wide
(`src/shell/Sidebar.styles.ts:9-14`); the top bar is a row that does not wrap, with a fixed search box of 300
(`src/shell/TopBar.styles.ts:8-27`); the card rows of screen 24 are always laid out horizontally
(`src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.styles.ts:11`, `blocks/TileRow.styles.ts:7`). The shape gate measures only
at 1280 and 1440 (`e2e/web/shape.spec.ts:7-12`) and Playwright has only a desktop configuration
(`playwright.config.ts`), so no gate saw it.

Minimum widths measured at 1440 (min-content of each block): metric tile 56 to 103 (eight tiles need about 773 px);
first card row 475 (English), 404 (Vietnamese); second row 466; third row 585, 559; the widest
card 226. The top bar needs about 713 px not counting the breadcrumb.

## Decisions (the controller, per FE-21)

Each decision: what, why, the price if it is wrong.

- **R-N1 Scope.** Spec 4.4 is for the page shell and screen 24 on the web; the same code runs on the iOS and Android app.
  Not done here: the safe area of the notch on the app (spec line 258, plan C), the Maestro flow, reference
  images. Why: the product owner reviews on a phone browser first. Price: the phone app keeps text lying
  under the status bar until plan C.
- **R-N2 Source of the width.** React Native's `useWindowDimensions()` through `tierOf(width)`: `desktop` from
  `bpDesktop` 1280, `tablet` from `bpTablet` 768, `phone` below that. Four new tokens in `brand/tokens.css`:
  `--bp-tablet: 768px`, `--bp-desktop: 1280px`, `--touch: 44px` (the minimum touch target of spec 4.4),
  `--rail-w: 64px` (icon rail: a touch target of 44 plus 10 on each side). Why: one mechanism for all three platforms (the app
  has no CSS media query), it updates itself when the device rotates or the window is resized. Price: two renders if the window
  is resized continuously; negligible.
- **R-N3 Desktop unchanged.** From 1280 every measurement stays unchanged; the layout measurement at 1280 and 1440 stays unchanged.
- **R-N4 Tablet.** The sidebar becomes an icon rail `railW` wide: a menu button at the top (it opens the full
  sidebar as a drawer), then one icon button for each link item of the three groups Home, Portfolio, Workspace
  (the accessible name is the label of the item; the count sits in the corner and in the name). Planned items and the project tree exist only in the
  drawer. The eight metric tiles become two rows of four tiles. The card rows stay as on desktop (measured: they fit at 656 px). The search box of the
  top bar can shrink. Why: spec 4.4. Price: the project tree needs two presses on a tablet.
- **R-N5 Phone.** No sidebar column. The top bar holds the menu button, the breadcrumb (cut with an
  ellipsis), the bell, the language selector; it hides the search box (already in the drawer), New, Help (not built yet, V2) and
  the avatar (decoration only). The eight metric tiles become four rows of two tiles; one card per row; every control has a
  touch target of at least 44 x 44. Why: spec 4.4; BRD D-19 asks only for viewing and light updates on the phone (Focus,
  Board, Overview, approval), so creating a new project is not needed on the phone. Price: if creating a project on the
  phone is wanted, add New to the drawer.
- **R-N6 Drawer.** React Native's `Modal`, transparent background, holding the whole `Sidebar` component (its
  content unchanged) and a dimmed backdrop button to close. It closes when: Escape is pressed (web), the Back button is pressed (Android), the dimmed backdrop is pressed,
  another page is navigated to, the window widens to the desktop tier. Why: react-native-web's Modal already keeps the focus
  inside, closes on Escape and returns the focus to the button that opened it
  (`node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Modal/ModalContent.js:26-35`,
  `ModalFocusTrap.js:66-118`); on the app it is the operating system's Modal. Price: no slide animation (add
  `animationType` later if the product owner wants it).
- **R-N7 Wrapping instead of a width tier when it suffices.** The project header (the title block has a minimum width
  `headerTitleMin`, the buttons wrap when space runs out), the tab row, the screen title row: add `flexWrap`, nothing
  changes on desktop because everything fits in one row there.
- **R-N8 Cards on the phone drop `flex: 1`.** In a column whose height follows its content, Yoga gives `flex: 1`
  a base size of 0 and does not share out the free space, so the cards shrink to 0 and pile on top of each other on the app
  [Source: `node_modules/react-native/ReactCommon/yoga/yoga/node/Node.cpp:329-339`,
  `algorithm/CalculateLayout.cpp:1640-1649`]. On the web CSS treats `flex-basis: 0%` in a frame with no definite
  height as `content`, so only the app is affected. Why: one mechanism that is right for both.
- **R-N9 Touch targets.** A hook `useTouch()` returns `{ minHeight: touch, minWidth: touch }` at the phone tier,
  `null` at other tiers; applied to Button, Segmented, Select, Menu, BarRow, the rows and the picker of the sidebar, the tabs
  of the header, the bell, the menu button. StackBar: the bar is `touch` tall on the phone; the width of each segment follows the
  data, so a segment narrower than 44 px stays narrow: a question for the product owner (whether the legend line may become a
  replacement link).
- **R-N10 Tests.** The default window of a component test is a 1440 x 900 desktop
  (`src/window.test.setup.ts`, only for the two Jest projects iOS and Android), because the React Native preset
  emulates a 750 px window, that is the phone tier (`node_modules/@react-native/jest-preset/jest/mocks/NativeModules.js`).
  A test that needs another tier sets `Dimensions.set` itself. Playwright adds `e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts`: 360 and 390
  (emulating a phone: `isMobile`, `hasTouch`), 768 and 1024, both languages, on Chromium and WebKit:
  no horizontal scrolling, the window is not shrunk by the browser, text is not cut, the grid of metric tiles and the cards have the right
  shape, touch targets of at least 44 on the phone, the drawer opens, closes on Escape and returns the focus to the menu button, navigating to
  another page closes it, axe has no errors of serious or critical level.

## Steps

1. Tokens: add the four tokens and `--header-title-min` to `brand/tokens.css`, run `pnpm gen:tokens`.
2. `src/design-system/tier.ts`: `tierOf`, `useTier`, `useTouch`; boundary tests 767, 768, 1279, 1280.
3. `src/window.test.setup.ts` and `jest.config.js` (setupFilesAfterEnv of the two native projects).
4. Touch targets and cards: Button, Segmented, Select, Menu, BarRow, StackBar, Card; CountBadge gains a corner position.
5. Shell: `MenuButton`, `Rail`, the drawer in `Shell`, the top bar by tier, the sidebar with touch targets,
   the project header wrapping and the tabs with touch targets; new text in `src/shell/strings`.
6. Screen 24: `TileRow` splits rows by tier, `Screen` one column on the phone, `HeaderRow` wraps.
7. `e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts`.
8. `pnpm verify` with all ten steps; retake the screenshots at phone and tablet width for the product owner.

Each step: write the test first, see it red, only then write the code.

## Rulings made during the run

- **R-N11 Status bar on the phone.** Measured after step 6: the "Waiting 1" segment of Meridian is 23
  to 27 px wide. Forcing every segment to a minimum width of 44 distorts the proportions (1 of 12 work items would look like 14%). Chosen:
  on the phone the segment is for looking only (`StackBar`), the legend line that has `href` is a touch-height link to
  the same destination (`Legend`, `StatusCard`); status 0 has no segment so its line is text. Replaces R-N9
  (touch-height bar). Price: on the phone the legend must be pressed, not the bar.
- **R-N12 Language selector.** WebKit keeps the `height` of the select tag and ignores `min-height` (measured on
  WebKit emulating iPhone 15: 44 x 30, the text squeezed into "Ti"). The selector uses `height: touch` on the
  phone and `flexShrink: 0` at every tier (the breadcrumb shrinks instead).
- **R-N13 Screen title row.** The title block, the freshness and the scope sentence need `flexShrink: 1` to shrink to fit
  the row (react-native-web gives View `flexShrink: 0`), otherwise it overflows to 584 to 621 px.
- **R-N14 Breadcrumb `flexGrow: 1`.** On the phone there is no longer a search box with `marginLeft: auto`
  to push the bell to the right. On desktop nothing visible changes (the search box is still evenly spaced as before).
- **R-N15 The tablet top bar drops Help** (not built yet, V2): at 768 px with the icon rail, the
  fixed parts need 694 px against the 656 px available.
- **R-N16 The clipped-text test** does not examine the top bar: the breadcrumb is deliberately cut with an ellipsis
  (`review.md` section 4), like `shape.spec.ts`. The two functions `overflowing` and `clipped` move from
  `shape.spec.ts` to `e2e/web/support.ts` to be shared.
- **R-N17 Reverse test of the new measurement.** Built a temporary copy in which `tierOf` always returns `desktop` (the old layout) in a scratch
  folder, ran `narrow.spec.ts` on Chromium: every phone case and the 768 px case red, with the window widened
  to 948 to 962 px (exactly the measurements of the defect), the 1024 px case red because the sidebar remains; the code was restored unchanged
  (compared with `cmp`).
- **R-N18 The file-editing tool changes characters in a file that has `\u` escape sequences.** In `Glyph.tsx` and
  `Glyph.test.native.tsx`, the tool wrote the Vietnamese comments as escape sequences (the letter "u" with an acute accent became `\u00FA`) and wrote
  the test's escape sequence `'\u2261'` as the real character; fixed again with a script and the bytes checked with `od -c`. When editing a file that has escape sequences, check the bytes.

### After the independent code review (09/10/2026)

A code review agent read 60 files and measured with Chromium on the build; seven points, each examined in turn:

- **R-N19 The drawer reopens by itself** (correct, measurable): open the drawer on Overview, press Registry, press Back and the drawer
  reopens, because `openAt` is cleared only when close is pressed. Fix: `useDrawer` remembers the page and the tier where the drawer opened, when one
  of the two changes it clears right in that render (no effect, no flicker). Consequence: rotating the device or resizing the
  window across a tier closes the drawer (replacing the old test that kept the drawer open from phone to tablet).
- **R-N20 The icon rail button name includes the count** (correct; R-N4 already stated it but the code did not do it): "My focus 9" like
  the sidebar row, because the number shown on the button must be part of the name (WCAG 2.5.3).
- **R-N21 The search box shrinks at the tablet tier** (correct; R-N4 already stated it but the code did not do it): at 768 px the breadcrumb
  has only 79 px left (English) and 84 px (Vietnamese) when the search box keeps 300. Desktop keeps 300 (layout measurement).
- **R-N22 The testID `rail-<code>` is read by no one** (correct): keep the testID (like `nav-<code>` of the sidebar, for
  Maestro later), add a test that reads it; Stryker on `Rail.tsx` goes up to 100%.
- **R-N23 Focus when the tier changes while the drawer is open** (correct, minor): the drawer closes (R-N19) and the button that opened it also
  disappears with the old tier, so the focus goes to `body`; react-native-web returns the focus only to an element still in
  the page (`Modal/ModalFocusTrap.js:111-120`). Accepted: it only happens when the device is rotated or the window is resized
  exactly while the drawer is open.
- **R-N24 The text of the search box in the drawer** (correct): centered vertically; desktop unchanged.
- **R-N25 Menu load error on the icon rail** (possible): the rail has only the menu button left, the error message shows when the
  drawer opens. Accepted as it is: an empty rail is the sign, the error message is one press away.

Check by the review agent: the full-page screenshots at 1440 px in both languages match the screenshots of 08/10/2026 pixel by pixel
(0 pixels differ over 1440 x 1160), meaning desktop is unchanged.

- **R-N26 The placeholder text of the search box on one line.** The 768 px screenshot taken after R-N21 shows that when the search box shrinks, the placeholder text
  wraps to three lines and the box is taller than the top bar. The old measurement did not see it (it left out the text of the top bar and measured only horizontal overflow).
  Add the measurement "every part of the top bar lies within the height of the bar" to `narrow.spec.ts`, run it and see red
  exactly the 768 px English case (`topbar-search`), then give the placeholder text `lines={1}` (cut with an ellipsis like
  the breadcrumb; on desktop the text fits in 300 px so nothing changes).

## Testing on iOS and Android emulators (09/10/2026, FE-25)

The product owner: "this machine still has an IOS simulator, so if anything is missing, install it to test fully". The app built
on this machine: iPhone 18 Pro (iOS 27), the Android virtual device `metis-pixel` (Pixel 7, Android 15) and
`metis-tablet` (Pixel Tablet in portrait, 800 dp, created in this round). Each defect below was seen on the emulators
but the web test suite does not see it; each defect has a measurement from before the fix and a test that is kept.

- **R-N27 Safe area** (spec line 258, earlier left for plan C): on the iPhone 18 Pro the status bar
  (62 points) overlaps the top bar, Maestro's press on the menu button lands on the status bar. The shell and the panel of the drawer
  take their margins from `useSafeAreaInsets` (`safeArea` in `Shell.styles.ts`); the test
  `Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx` with the measurements of that device (62 at the top, 34 at the bottom).
- **R-N28 Project name block `minWidth: headerTitleMin` (240).** Yoga on iOS ignores `flexBasis` when the
  header row wraps: the name block is down to 63 points, the action buttons stay on the same row.
- **R-N29 Language selector on iOS** (`Select.ios.tsx`): the native iOS picker is a wheel 216 points tall,
  on the top bar only an empty frame remains. The button shows the current choice and the open mark; pressing it opens the iOS
  selection sheet (`ActionSheetIOS`), the title is the label, the cancel button takes its text from the dictionary (`topbar.cancel`); the accessible name is
  "Language, English" (WCAG 2.5.3).
- **R-N30 Language selector on Android** (`Select.android.tsx`): the native picker is 37 pixels wide, shows
  no text, its arrow overlaps the bell button (measured with `uiautomator dump`). The frame is the same as the iOS version; the native picker
  covers the whole frame with `opacity` 0,01. Not 0: Android treats an element with alpha 0 as not shown, Maestro does not
  find the id `language` (measured), and screen readers skip it too. Do not use a transparent color: the arrow is tinted
  in the SRC_ATOP way (`ReactPicker.setDropdownIconColor`), a transparent color leaves the arrow as it is (measured: the arrow
  still overlaps the text "English"). The title of the selection dialog is the label (`prompt`).
- **R-N31 Dark status bar text** (`Shell.tsx`): Android leaves white text on the transparent bar, the time and
  the battery are invisible on a white background. `StatusBar.setBarStyle('dark-content')` in an effect of the shell,
  not the `StatusBar` component: that component calls `clearImmediate`, which the jsdom environment of Stryker does not
  have (measured: the first trial run of Stryker was red with `ReferenceError`). The phone flow was run with the device in dark
  mode on both platforms: the app stays on a light background, the status bar text is dark, the selection sheet of the operating system follows dark
  mode and is still readable.
- **R-N32 Fonts on Android.** The three font files are variable fonts (one file holding every weight); React
  Native on Android draws only the default weight of the file (Manrope is 200, Inter and Newsreader are 400). Measured the stroke
  thickness divided by the text height on screenshots, iOS against Android before the fix: button 0,111 and 0,071; tab
  0,103 and 0,038; the number of the metric tile 0,177 and 0,130; after the fix Android is 0,143, 0,115, 0,185 (ordinary Inter text
  as the reference: 0,107 and 0,125). Fix: nine static files (three fonts, weights 400, 500, 600) cut with
  `fonttools varLib.instancer <font>.ttf wght=<weight> --static` into `assets/fonts/android`, declared as
  XML font families of the `expo-font` plugin (`app.json`); `fonts.android.ts` does not load fonts at run time. iOS and
  web keep the variable files. Test `scripts/native-fonts.test.mjs`: the files are static, the weight written in the file
  matches the declared weight.
- **R-N33 The "·" mark of the project info line** (`ProjectHeader.tsx`): when the line wraps, the mark before the stage
  label hangs at the end of the line (measured on the web at 360, 390, 768; seen on iOS and Android too). The mark becomes a child
  positioned absolutely flush against the left of the item that follows it, the row has `overflow: hidden`: when the later item wraps to the start of a line
  the mark goes out past the left edge and is cut. Spacing 9,6 pixels, mark, 9 against 10, mark, 10 in the wireframe.
  The `narrow.spec.ts` measurement ("the info line of the header"), with a check that the mark is really cut using
  `elementFromPoint`; reverse test: removing `overflow: hidden` makes it red ("stray").
- **R-N34 Text laid out like iOS and Android.** In a row, Yoga's text does not shrink (`flexShrink` 0), the web's
  text shrinks according to CSS: on an Android tablet the sentence "3 of 12 work items done" of the progress card overflows 41
  pixels out of the card. Fix: the sentence sits in a `flexShrink: 1` frame (`ProgressCard`). New gate in
  `narrow.spec.ts`: the web version forces text to be laid out like Yoga (`flex-shrink: 0` and `max-width: 100%`, because Yoga measures text
  within the width of the containing frame) and then demands that no text passes the edge of an ancestor frame, at 360, 390, 768, 800, 900,
  1024, 1279 and 1440, both languages, also when the drawer is open. Without `max-width` the emulation also reports
  text standing alone in a row (the health warning frame), whereas on a real device that text wraps correctly. Reverse
  test: removing the fix makes 6 cases red (768, 800, 900).
- **R-N35 App icon** (spec 5.2 and the brand gate "app icon is the right file", missed by plan B): iOS and
  Android still had the sample icon of Expo. Now taken from `brand/logo`: iOS uses the square version
  (`metis-app-icon-square`), because the pre-rounded app icon is flattened by Expo onto a white background (measured: pixel 2,2 of
  the iOS icon is white); Android uses an adaptive icon: an ink-colored background, the foreground is the letter M and the diamond scaled to 2/3
  around the center (`metis-app-icon-android-foreground`), because with the whole app icon as the foreground the round mask cuts off the feet of
  the letter M (the corner of the letter is 45 dp from the center, the visible circle has a radius of 36 dp). These two versions are generated with
  `brand/tools/platform-icons.mjs`; a byte-for-byte copy is in `assets/brand`; the test
  `scripts/brand-files.test.mjs`.
- **R-N36 Splash screen:** from the blue background and the Expo logo to an ink-colored background with the foreground of the Android icon
  (`imageWidth` 200).
- **R-N37 App name "Metis"** (the Expo template leaves "metis" in lower case under the icon). The generated iOS project is renamed to match:
  `ios/Metis.xcworkspace`, scheme `Metis`.
- **R-N38 Android tablet:** the virtual device `metis-tablet` created from the system image `android-35` that was already available; the flow
  `e2e/native/tablet.yaml` (icon rail, drawer opened from the menu button of the rail, navigation from the rail). iPad
  NOT RUN: `ios.supportsTablet` is not turned on yet, the iPad opens the app in iPhone compatibility mode (a question for the product
  owner).
- **R-N39 Jest test for the web version of the selector** (`Select.test.web.tsx`, rendered with react-dom into jsdom):
  since Android has its own file, no test runs `Select.tsx` (unit gate red: coverage 99,34%).
  Install `@types/react-dom` 19.2.7 as a development dependency (error:
  `TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module 'react-dom/client'`).
- **R-N40 Metro run with `CI=1` does not reload by itself** (log: "Metro is running in CI mode, reloads are
  disabled"): after each copy of the code to the native build Metro must be restarted. This corrects the earlier note
  that held the cause to be a missing watchman.
- **R-N41 The test suite must not overload the machine** (FE-26): twice in one day the 10-core Mac was overloaded because
  Stryker opened 9 test processes and Jest opened 9 child processes, each near 100% CPU, at times overlapping
  (load 21). Limits in the repo: `concurrency: "50%"` in `stryker.config.json` (Stryker runs Jest with
  `runInBand: true`, so the number of processes of the mutation testing step equals exactly this number), `maxWorkers: '50%'`
  in `jest.config.js`, and `scripts/verify.mjs` and `scripts/canary.mjs` call
  `setPriority(constants.priority.PRIORITY_LOW)` before running the gates (child processes inherit it). Measured: Stryker
  "Creating 5 test runner process(es)", Jest at most 5 child processes, the `tsc` of `gate:types` runs at
  nice 19. Playwright by default already used half the number of cores. On a 4-core CI, Stryker is left with 2 test processes:
  CI has not run even once and the 30-minute limit of the job is already shorter than one full mutation testing run.

### After the independent code review of the emulator round (09/10/2026 evening)

A code review agent read the code of this round (read only, did not run the test suite) and reported ten points; each point was examined on
the real code:

- **R-N42 Touch target 44 on the app at every width** (correct; spec 7, accessibility gate, iOS and
  Android column: "touch target of at least 44 x 44", the reverse test at spec line 472): the app had touch-size targets only at the phone
  tier, so the Android tablet had controls 18 to 30 dp tall. Fix: `fingerOnly` in
  `design-system/pointer.ts` (true on the app) and `pointer.web.ts` (false on the web); `useTouchTargets` in
  `tier.ts` is the phone or `fingerOnly`, `useTouch` uses it; the language selector, the segments of the status bar
  (`StackBar`) and the search box of the top bar use the same condition. The component test measures both modes: it fakes
  `fingerOnly` with a variable `mockFingerOnly` (the rule of the web) or leaves it alone (the rule of the app). Measured on the virtual device
  with `uiautomator dump` across both the page and the drawer, each element taking its largest size over the scrolls: the tablet
  of 800 dp with the old rule 41 of 75 elements smaller than 44 dp (the row of the work item card 18, the Raise change
  request button 26, the language selector 30, the sidebar item 28), with the new rule 0 of 75; the Android 15 phone and
  Android 7.0 both 0 of 62.
- **R-N43 Name of the language selector on Android** (correct): the native picker has only the label "Language", and that label hides
  the text of the selected item from TalkBack. The name is now "Language, English" like the iOS version. The border of the frame moved into the
  inner shape: Yoga places an absolutely positioned child inside the border of the containing frame, so before that the picker was only
  42 tall out of 44.
- **R-N44 Fonts by weight on Android 7 to 8.1** (correct; spec line 383 supports from Android 7): below
  Android 9 React Native distinguishes only regular text and bold 700 text within a font family
  (`ReactFontManager.kt`, `TypefaceStyle.apply` uses `nearestStyle`), so an XML font family with many weights draws 500
  and 600 with the 400 file. Fix: each weight is its own family ("Inter-500"), nine families in `app.json`;
  `design-system/fontFace.android.ts` renames the family by the final weight of the text (`Text.tsx`), the iOS and web versions
  stay unchanged. Measured on the virtual device `metis-api24` (Android 7.0, created in this round): the stroke thickness ratio of the button
  0,143, tab 0,115, number 0,182, equal to Android 15.
- **R-N45 Project info line**: the three frames wrapping client, PM, stage have `flexShrink: 1`, because the View of
  react-native-web does not shrink by default, a long name is cut off by overflow (the new measurement replaces the text right on the page
  with a 58-character name at 360 px); the "·" mark is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`), because it is only for
  decoration and at times lies outside the edge of the row.
- **R-N46 Equivalent mutant in the empty dependency array** of the status bar effect (`[]` becoming another constant array
  still runs the effect once): a comment that disables the mutant, with the reason, following the pattern of `useOverview.ts`.
- **R-N47 Three gaps in the tests**: the cancel button of the iOS selection sheet takes its text from the dictionary (new test in
  `TopBar.test.native.tsx`); the left and right margins of the safe area are not swapped (a device with a cutout on the left,
  `Shell.safeArea.test.native.tsx`); the two derived icon versions carry exactly the strokes of the original app icon
  (`brand-files.test.mjs`). Two test files went over the 300-line ceiling so the shared builder functions moved to
  `Shell.test.helper.tsx` and `ProjectHeader.test.helper.tsx`.
- **Keyboard focus ring of the selector on Android** (not yet verified): not a spec item of the native app
  (the focus ring is a web gate), recorded in the review package, not fixed.
- **R-N48 Not overloading the machine, the remainder** (FE-26): besides Stryker and Jest, the web gate with 5 browsers
  pushed the load up to 21, now Playwright `workers: '30%'` and Metro builds the web version with `--max-workers 4` (measured: highest load
  9,2 in the web gate). A native rebuild from scratch (`prebuild --clean`) recompiles the C++ code with ninja with a number of
  processes equal to the number of cores plus two, outside the `--max-workers` limit of Gradle (measured: load 25): rebuild only when
  the native configuration changes. A cold boot of the iPhone simulator pushes the load up to 77 for a moment. The repo lives in
  iCloud Drive, so each test run inside the repo generates thousands of files for the sync process
  `fileproviderd` (measured: 34% CPU, state "stuck"; three temporary copies of Stryker left behind, 979 files): `pnpm
  verify` runs in the copy `~/metis-run/verify` outside iCloud (rsync of the repo, `pnpm install
  --frozen-lockfile`), the report is copied back.
- **Android tablet in landscape** (measured): the app, locked to portrait, is squeezed by Android into a box in the middle of the screen about
  600 dp wide, using the phone layout and with the guidance box of the operating system
  (`apps/metis/reports/review/native/android-tablet-landscape-letterbox.png`); a question for the product owner.

How to run (the native build is outside iCloud, the generated `ios/` folder weighs 1,2 GB):

1. Copy `app.json`, `assets/`, `src/`, `e2e/native/` to `~/metis-run/native/apps/metis`, then
   `CI=1 pnpm exec expo prebuild --clean --platform all` there.
2. iOS: `xcodebuild -workspace ios/Metis.xcworkspace -scheme Metis -configuration Debug -sdk
   iphonesimulator -derivedDataPath ios/build build`, then `xcrun simctl install`. Android:
   `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21 ./gradlew app:assembleDebug -PreactNativeDevServerPort=8091
   -PreactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a`, `adb reverse tcp:8091 tcp:8091`, `adb install -r`.
3. Metro: `CI=1 EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS=1 pnpm exec expo start --port 8091`.
4. `maestro --device <device> test e2e/native/{smoke,phone,tablet}.yaml` (Maestro needs `JAVA_HOME` like
   Gradle).

Final result (the code after all the rulings above, up to R-N48): on iOS the startup flow of 5 steps and the phone flow of 23
steps are green; Android 15 phone and Android 7.0 green likewise; the Android tablet in portrait 15 steps green;
the phone flow in dark mode green on iOS and Android (run before R-N42). Measurements of touch targets and font weight
on the virtual devices: R-N42, R-N44. Evidence: `apps/metis/reports/native/narrow/{ios,android,android7}/`, selected
screenshots at `apps/metis/reports/review/native/`.

The real run of this round: `pnpm verify` in the copy `~/metis-run/verify` outside iCloud, ten gates green,
mutation testing 99,93% (1.415 caught, 15 timed out, 1 survived: the equivalent mutant of R-N46, the comment disabling
the mutant, placed at the end of the function body, has no effect, so it was changed into the pair `Stryker disable` and `Stryker restore`
around `useEffect`; 75 minutes with 5 processes). After that fix: mutation testing run separately on `Shell.tsx` 100%,
the other ten gates rerun green (2.663 unit tests, coverage 100%, 160 browser tests).
Load during the full run: median 8,9, highest 17,9 (`apps/metis/reports/verify.md`).
